actionRationale: Strong multi-source spread and an obvious visual product, but no demand evidence and possibly near peak. Build the sticker pack on free platforms quickly; add the printable only if stickers draw favorites.

adopters.text: Global TikTok/Reels/X meme accounts in several languages, a pop-culture outlet, an airline brand account, and Spanish and Portuguese-language media and creators.

competition.text: A web search found only generic Chilean flag apparel, no meme-specific products. Marketplaces were not checked directly.

gap.text: Cute illustrated 'stretched objects' stickers and a field-guide style poster that turn the meme into a design object, with no flags, crests or brand references.

name: Chile memes (everything is narrow)

origin.text: Earlier sporadic jokes; the current wave started with a Sept 18, 2026 TikTok ('How I still imagine Chile') at 2.3M views in five days.

productDemand.text: No purchase evidence; engagement is entertainment and curiosity.

products.differentiation: Cohesive illustrated set rather than flag souvenirs or screenshots
products.pivotIf: Interest only in 1-2 objects: expand those into a series
products.rightsNote: No coat of arms, seals, sports crests, brands or real people
products.stopIf: No sales and under 5 favorites after 14 days
products.theme: Illustrated sticker pack of everyday objects stretched tall and narrow ('everything here is narrow')
products.validationTest: 10 designs on Redbubble; 6 short videos in 2 weeks
products.whyBuy: Signals being in on the meme with a cute, giftable design

products.buyer: Meme fans, students and geography teachers
products.differentiation: Design-led 'science plate' look instead of a meme screenshot
products.pivotIf: Pins saved but no sales: sell as a phone wallpaper pack
products.theme: Vintage field-guide printable of 12 narrow 'specimens' with a Chile-outline ruler
products.validationTest: Launch after stickers get favorites; 3 weeks on Etsy + Pinterest
products.whyBuy: Funny dorm/classroom wall art that outlasts the spike

rights.note: A country's shape and name are free to use. Avoid coat of arms, government seals, sports crests and kits, and brand references (including the airline that joined). Keep the tone affectionate.

productFit.rationale: Highly visual joke suits stickers and posters

supplyGap.rationale: No meme-specific products found via search

timing.rationale: Surge began Sept 18; may already be near first peak

spread.text: Independent coverage from Know Your Meme, Thunder Dungeon, The Brew News, a Brazilian outlet, Complex on X and a Spanish-language YouTube explainer within about 10 days; runner-up in KYM's September vote.

summary: A September 2026 surge of jokes imagining that everything in Chile, from buses to soccer fields, is as long and narrow as the country.

trajectory.text: About two weeks old, spreading fast across languages; a brand joining on Sept 24 suggests it may already be near its first peak. No product supply was found. Fast-moving: it could become early growth or fade within weeks.

unresolved: Are new Chile posts still appearing at volume after Oct 10?
Do Chilean creators embrace it (positive) or push back (negative)?
Any Chile-meme merch appearing on Redbubble/Etsy?
what: Creators post images and videos of everyday objects stretched tall and thin, captioned like 'How I still imagine Chile'. The joke had existed in small form since about 2020 but exploded on TikTok and Reels from Sept 18, 2026, spread across languages, and pulled in at least one brand post.

invalidators: Sharp drop in new posts by mid-October
Chilean backlash framing the joke as mocking
window.reasoning: Visual country jokes can recur (KYM compares it to Ohio memes), but the current spike started Sept 18 and brand participation often signals a near-peak. Illustrated products can keep selling to geography-humor buyers.
